fullPassage:
Letters from Recent Graduates

Welcome to a new season of High School Magazine. To start off the new school year on the right foot, we asked some of our recent graduates to give us tips on how to succeed in the coming year and beyond.

Compare Apples to Apples
Nahyeon Kim Class of 2024

In high school, everyone told me how talented an artist I was, so I dreamed of becoming an illustrator. In university, though, everyone seemed much more talented than me, and they all worked so hard that I felt small in comparison. I thought about giving up my dream of becoming an artist. Then one day, I happened to see a drawing I had won an award for from middle school on the kitchen wall. I was embarrassed because it wasn't very good.

People say you shouldn't compare apples to oranges, and they're right. That's why it doesn't make sense to compare yourself to Internet personalities or even people in your real life. Maybe they had an advantage, or even a disadvantage, that you didn't. If you are going to compare yourself to anyone, the only fair comparison is "yesterday-you." Only you know where you started and how much effort you've put in. I couldn't see the progress in my ability when I only compared myself to others. Everyone develops differently. I'm able to see now the drawing in the kitchen was full of mistakes that I no longer make. It is empowering to see how I have improved rather than to envy the success of others. Your competition isn't the person next door or the influencer on social media: it's you.

Don't Be Afraid to Speak Up
Elias Walter Class of 2025

Do you share your opinion in class discussions, or do you just stay silent and keep it to yourself? Like many of you, I often found myself in the second group. A little black hole inside of me swallowed my voice when I considered speaking up. The consequences of being ridiculed or being wrong were always on my mind.

Then, after a particularly heated conversation in class, I asked myself, "What am I afraid of?" I was scared that bad things would happen, but I never thought about good things. When I noticed others taking risks, I knew that I needed to do the same in order to participate. Many people are scared to speak up, but a lot of them do it anyway because they think it's worth it. So I left my comfort zone and started to speak up. I grew intellectually and socially by expressing myself more clearly. I got closer to friends who liked how open I was with them. Now I have more people with whom I can talk, share my ideas, and learn new things. Remember, taking the risk of expressing yourself can be extremely rewarding in unexpected ways.

Use Energy on What You Can Control
Abigail Princeton Class of 2022

As I worked through my second year into my third in college, I had more troubles balancing school and personal life. I would get excited, anxious, worried, and bored all at once and then separately. I would get exhausted when I had to write a report for my courses, mediate a disaster between friends, and respond to the comments on my online journal. I was drowning in a sea of responsibilities, concerns, and anxieties, and that was when I read an article with a simple insight.

The article advised me to draw two big circles, with myself in the center. The smaller circle is my circle of influence, and I have direct control over the things inside it: what I eat and drink, how I behave, or what I do after school. The bigger circle is called my circle of concern: things I worry about but have no direct control over. For example, I have no direct control over how my professor will react to my report, but I do have control over the amount of research I do for it. Believing that everything was in my circle of influence left me stressed out and constantly exhausted. By wasting less energy on my circle of concern, I was able to invest more energy into things that mattered. I no longer worry about what my friends think, and I focus on my own actions. I don't get anxious over what might be on the test, and instead I put in every effort to understand the concepts themselves. Now, I only put my mental and physical energy into my circle of influence: eating healthy, staying in shape, and working hard.

questions.passage: In high school, everyone told me how talented an artist I was, so I dreamed of becoming an illustrator. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 그림이 별로 좋지 않았기(wasn't) 때문에 부끄러웠다. isn't → wasn't (과거 시제 일치)
det.analysis:
✅ ④ isn't → wasn't: 주절이 과거(was embarrassed)이므로 종속절도 과거 시제 필요
❌ ① felt: 과거형 정상
❌ ② giving: 전치사 about + 동명사 정상
❌ ③ won: 과거완료(had won) 정상
det.tip: 시제 일치: 과거 주절(was embarrassed) → 종속절도 과거(wasn't). 현재형 isn't는 불가

questions.passage: Do you share your opinion in class discussions, or do you just stay silent and keep it to yourself? Like many of you, I often ①<u>found</u> myself in the second group. A little black hole inside of me swallowed my voice when I ②<u>considered</u> speaking up. Then, after a particularly heated conversation in class, I asked ③<u>me</u>, 'What am I afraid of?' I was scared that bad things ④<u>would</u> happen.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 나는 나 자신에게(myself) 물었다. me → myself (재귀대명사)
det.analysis:
✅ ③ me → myself: 주어 I와 목적어가 같은 사람이므로 재귀대명사 myself 필요. asked myself
❌ ① found: 과거형 정상 (found myself)
❌ ② considered: 과거형 정상
❌ ④ would: 과거 시점의 추측 (was scared that ~ would) 정상
det.tip: 주어와 목적어가 같은 사람이면 재귀대명사 사용. I asked myself = 나 자신에게 물었다

questions.passage: The article advised me to draw two big circles, with myself in the center. The smaller circle is my circle of influence, and I have direct control over the things inside it. For example, I have no direct control over how my professor will react to my report, but I do have control over the amount of research I do for it. ①<u>Believing</u> that everything was in my circle of influence left me ②<u>stressing</u> out and constantly ③<u>exhausted</u>. By wasting less energy on my circle of concern, I was able ④<u>to invest</u> more energy into things that mattered.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 모든 것이 나의 영향력의 원 안에 있다고 믿는 것은 나를 스트레스 받게(stressed) 만들었다. stressing → stressed (감정 수동)
det.analysis:
✅ ② stressing → stressed: left me stressed out. 사람이 스트레스를 '받는' 것이므로 과거분사(수동). left + O + 과거분사(OC)
❌ ① Believing: 동명사 주어 정상
❌ ③ exhausted: 과거분사 (피곤해진 상태) 정상
❌ ④ to invest: was able to V 정상
det.tip: 감정 동사의 분사: -ing(감정 유발), -ed(감정 경험). stressed out = 스트레스 받은 상태

questions.passage: Welcome to a new season of High School Magazine. To start off the new school year on the right foot, we asked some of our recent ①<u>graduates</u> to give us tips on how to ②<u>succeed</u> in the coming year and beyond. In high school, everyone told me how ③<u>talented</u> an artist I was, so I dreamed of becoming an illustrator. In university, though, everyone seemed much more talented than me, and I felt small in ④<u>harmony</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 나는 비교해서(comparison) 작게 느꼈다. harmony(조화)는 comparison(비교)과 다른 의미이므로 부적절하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ harmony(조화) → comparison(비교)이 원문. 다른 사람보다 못하다고 느끼는 문맥에 harmony는 부적절
❌ ① graduates(졸업생): 원문 그대로
❌ ② succeed(성공하다): 원문 그대로
❌ ③ talented(재능 있는): 원문 그대로
det.tip: in comparison = 비교해서. in harmony = 조화 속에서. 문맥: 다른 사람보다 작게 느끼는 것 → comparison

questions.passage: Many people are scared to speak up, but a lot of them do it anyway because they think it's ①<u>worth</u> it. So I left my comfort zone and started to speak up. I grew intellectually and socially by expressing myself more clearly. I got closer to friends who liked how ②<u>open</u> I was with them. Now I have more people with whom I can talk, share my ideas, and learn new things. Remember, taking the risk of expressing yourself can be extremely ③<u>punishing</u> in ④<u>unexpected</u> ways.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 자신을 표현하는 위험을 감수하는 것은 극도로 보람 있을(rewarding) 수 있다. punishing(고통스러운)은 rewarding(보람 있는)의 반의어이므로 부적절하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ punishing(고통스러운) → rewarding(보람 있는)이 원문. 지적/사회적 성장이라는 긍정적 결과에 punishing은 부적절
❌ ① worth(가치 있는): 원문 그대로
❌ ② open(개방적인): 원문 그대로
❌ ④ unexpected(예상치 못한): 원문 그대로
det.tip: rewarding(보람 있는) ↔ punishing(고통스러운). 긍정적 결과를 서술하는 문맥에 주의

questions.passage: I couldn't see the progress in my ability when I only compared myself to others. Everyone develops differently. I'm able to see now the drawing in the kitchen was full of mistakes that I no longer make. It is empowering to see how I have improved rather than to __________ the success of others. Your competition isn't the person next door or the influencer on social media: it's you.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 다른 사람의 성공을 부러워하기(envy)보다 내가 얼마나 발전했는지 보는 것이 힘을 준다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② envy(부러워하다): 원문 그대로. rather than to envy = ~을 부러워하기보다
❌ ① celebrate(축하하다): 대조의 의미가 약해짐
❌ ③ ignore(무시하다): 문맥에 맞지 않음
❌ ④ achieve(달성하다): 타인의 성공을 달성한다는 것은 어색
det.tip: envy = 부러워하다, 시기하다. rather than to envy = ~을 시기하기보다는. improved ↔ envy 대조

questions.passage: I would get exhausted when I had to write a report for my courses, mediate a disaster between friends, and respond to the comments on my online journal. I was drowning in a sea of responsibilities, concerns, and anxieties, and that was when I read an article with a simple insight. By wasting less energy on my circle of concern, I was able to invest more energy into things that mattered. Now, I only put my mental and physical energy into my circle of __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 이제 나는 정신적, 신체적 에너지를 나의 영향력(influence)의 원에만 투입한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ influence: 원문 그대로. 통제 가능한 것(먹기, 운동, 노력)에 집중
❌ ① concern: 관심의 원은 에너지를 낭비하는 영역
❌ ② anxiety: 불안은 관심의 원에 해당
❌ ③ competition: 이 글의 주제와 무관
det.tip: circle of influence = 내가 통제할 수 있는 영역. 결론: 통제 가능한 것에만 에너지를 쏟는다

questions.passage: In high school, everyone told me how talented an artist I was, so I dreamed of becoming an illustrator. In university, though, everyone seemed much more talented than me, and they all worked so hard that I felt small in comparison. I thought about giving up my dream of becoming an artist. Then one day, I happened to see a drawing I had won an award for from middle school on the kitchen wall.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: 나현은 부엌 벽에서 중학교 때 상을 받은 그림을 우연히 보았다.
나현은 대학에서 가장 재능 있는 예술가로 인정받았다.

det.korean: 부엌 벽에서 중학교 때 상 받은 그림을 우연히 보았다(happened to see).
det.analysis:
✅ ① 우연히 보았다: 'happened to see a drawing I had won an award for' 원문 일치
❌ ② 대학에서 가장 재능 있는: 대학에서는 모두가 더 재능 있어 보였음
❌ ③ 고등학교 때 포기: 대학에서 포기를 생각했음
❌ ④ 중학교 때 삽화가: 꿈을 꾼 것이지 된 것은 아님
det.tip: happen to V = 우연히 ~하다. 우연히 그림을 본 것이 전환점이 됨

questions.passage: So I left my comfort zone and started to speak up. I grew intellectually and socially by expressing myself more clearly. I got closer to friends who liked how open I was with them. Now I have more people with whom I can talk, share my ideas, and learn new things.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: Elias는 말하기 시작한 후 친구들과 멀어졌다.
Elias는 자신의 의견을 숨기는 것이 더 나았다고 결론지었다.
Elias는 자신을 더 명확히 표현하면서 지적, 사회적으로 성장했다.

det.korean: Elias는 자신을 더 명확히 표현하면서 지적으로, 사회적으로 성장했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 지적/사회적 성장: 'grew intellectually and socially by expressing myself more clearly' 원문 일치
❌ ① 친구와 멀어짐: 'got closer to friends' 오히려 가까워짐
❌ ② 의견 숨기기: 말하기를 시작했으므로 반대
❌ ④ 안전지대 유지: 'left my comfort zone' 벗어남
det.tip: grew intellectually and socially = 지적으로 사회적으로 성장. 말하기 시작한 긍정적 결과

questions.passage: The article advised me to draw two big circles, with myself in the center. The smaller circle is my circle of influence, and I have direct control over the things inside it: what I eat and drink, how I behave, or what I do after school. The bigger circle is called my circle of concern: things I worry about but have no direct control over. For example, I have no direct control over how my professor will react to my report, but I do have control over the amount of research I do for it.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: Abigail은 기사에서 두 개의 큰 원을 그리라는 조언을 받았다.
영향력의 원에는 자신이 직접 통제할 수 있는 것이 포함된다.
보고서를 위한 조사량은 통제 가능한 영역이다.

det.korean: 원문: 교수의 반응은 직접 통제할 수 없는(no direct control over) 것으로, 관심의 원에 속한다. 영향력의 원이 아님.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 교수 반응은 영향력의 원: 원문에 'I have no direct control over how my professor will react'이므로 concern에 해당
❌ ① 두 원 조언: 'The article advised me to draw two big circles' 일치
❌ ③ 영향력의 원: 'I have direct control over the things inside it' 일치
❌ ④ 조사량 통제: 'I do have control over the amount of research' 일치
det.tip: 교수 반응(concern) vs 조사량(influence). 통제 가능 여부로 구분하는 것이 핵심

questions.passage: Do you share your opinion in class discussions, or do you just stay silent and keep it to yourself? A little black hole inside of me swallowed my voice when I considered speaking up. The consequences of being ridiculed or being wrong were always on my mind. Many people are scared to speak up, but a lot of them do it anyway because they think it's worth it. So I left my comfort zone and started to speak up. I grew intellectually and socially by expressing myself more clearly. Remember, taking the risk of expressing yourself can be extremely rewarding in unexpected ways.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 두려움을 극복하고 자신의 의견을 말하는 것은 보람 있는 일이다.
수업 토론에서 침묵을 유지하는 것이 안전한 선택이다.
조롱당할 위험을 피하는 것이 현명한 판단이다.
친구 관계는 자신의 의견을 숨길 때 더 좋아진다.

det.korean: 자신을 표현하는 위험을 감수하는 것은 예상치 못한 방식으로 극도로 보람 있을 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 두려움 극복: 핵심 메시지 'extremely rewarding in unexpected ways'
❌ ② 침묵 유지: 반대로 speak up을 권장
❌ ③ 위험 회피: 위험을 감수하라는 메시지
❌ ④ 의견 숨기기: speak up의 반대
det.tip: 핵심: taking the risk of expressing yourself can be extremely rewarding

questions.passage: People say you shouldn't compare apples to oranges, and they're right. That's why it doesn't make sense to compare yourself to Internet personalities or even people in your real life. If you are going to compare yourself to anyone, the only fair comparison is 'yesterday-you.' Only you know where you started and how much effort you've put in. Everyone develops differently. It is empowering to see how I have improved rather than to envy the success of others.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 공정한 경쟁을 위한 사회적 제도의 필요성
자기 자신의 성장에 초점을 맞추는 것의 중요성

det.korean: 자신을 타인이 아닌 '어제의 나'와 비교하고, 자기 성장에 초점을 맞추라는 내용이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ 자기 성장에 초점: 'the only fair comparison is yesterday-you', 'empowering to see how I have improved'
❌ ① 인터넷 유명인 위험성: 단순한 예시일 뿐
❌ ② 사회적 제도: 개인적 조언이지 사회 제도 이야기가 아님
❌ ③ 타인 성공 축하: envy하지 말라는 것이지 축하 방법이 아님
det.tip: compare yourself to 'yesterday-you' = 핵심 주제. 자기 성장 관점

questions.passage: People say you shouldn't compare apples to oranges, and they're right. That's why it doesn't make sense to compare yourself to Internet personalities or even people in your real life. Maybe they had an advantage, or even a disadvantage, that you didn't. <u>If you are going to compare yourself to anyone, the only fair comparison is "yesterday-you."</u>
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 밑줄 친 문장이 함축하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 과거의 실수를 반복하지 않도록 주의해야 한다.
타인의 장점을 배워 자신의 단점을 보완해야 한다.
자신의 성장은 타인이 아닌 과거의 자신과 비교해야만 공정하게 평가할 수 있다.

det.korean: 자신을 비교할 유일하게 공정한 대상은 '어제의 나'뿐이다 = 자기 성장의 공정한 기준은 과거의 자신이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 공정한 평가: the only fair comparison = 유일하게 공정한 비교. 타인은 조건이 다르므로 공정하지 않다는 맥락
❌ ① 실수 반복: 실수 방지가 아니라 성장 평가 기준
❌ ② 타인 장점 배우기: 타인과 비교하지 말라는 메시지
❌ ④ 실패 판정: 비교 기준이지 실패 판정이 아님
det.tip: the only fair comparison = 유일하게 공정한 비교. 조건이 다른 타인과의 비교는 불공정

questions.passage: Do you share your opinion in class discussions, or do you just stay silent and keep it to yourself? Like many of you, I often found myself in <u>the second group</u>. A little black hole inside of me swallowed my voice when I considered speaking up. The consequences of being ridiculed or being wrong were always on my mind. Then, after a particularly heated conversation in class, I asked myself, 'What am I afraid of?'
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 the second group이 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 토론에 참여하지 않고 교실을 떠나는 사람들

det.korean: 첫 번째 = 의견을 나누는 사람, 두 번째 = 침묵하며 의견을 간직하는 사람(stay silent and keep it to yourself).
det.analysis:
✅ ② 침묵 그룹: 'stay silent and keep it to yourself'가 the second group
❌ ① 적극 발언 그룹: 이것은 첫 번째 그룹
❌ ③ 비판 그룹: 언급 없음
❌ ④ 교실 이탈: 언급 없음
det.tip: or로 나눈 두 그룹: share opinion(1st) vs stay silent(2nd). the second group = 침묵 그룹

questions.passage: The article advised me to draw two big circles, with myself in the center. The smaller circle is my circle of influence, and I have direct control over the things inside it: what I eat and drink, how I behave, or what I do after school. The bigger circle is called my circle of concern: things I worry about but have no direct control over. For example, I have no direct control over how my professor will react to my report, but I do have control over the amount of research I do for <u>it</u>. Believing that everything was in my circle of influence left me stressed out and constantly exhausted.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 it이 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 나는 보고서(my report)를 위한 조사량을 통제할 수 있다. it = my report.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 보고서: 'the amount of research I do for it' → it = my report. 보고서를 위한 조사
❌ ② 영향력의 원: 조사 대상이 아님
❌ ③ 관심의 원: 조사 대상이 아님
❌ ④ 교수의 반응: 반응을 위해 조사하는 것이 아님
det.tip: it의 지칭: 가장 가까운 명사 my report. 'research I do for it' = 보고서를 위한 조사

questions.passage: I grew intellectually and socially by expressing myself more clearly. I got closer to friends who liked how open I was with them.
questions.stem:
위 글에서 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 **영어** 단어를 찾아 쓰시오.

"Elias는 자신을 더 명확하게 표현함으로써 지적으로 그리고 __________으로 성장했다."

det.korean: 지적으로 그리고 사회적으로(socially) 성장했다.
det.analysis: 원문 'grew intellectually and socially'에서 socially를 찾아 쓰는 문제.
det.tip: socially = 사회적으로. social(형용사) → socially(부사). intellectually and socially = 지적으로 그리고 사회적으로

questions.passage: Believing that everything was in my circle of influence left me stressed out and constantly exhausted. By __________ (waste) less energy on my circle of concern, I was able to invest more energy into things that mattered.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: 관심의 원에 에너지를 덜 낭비함으로써(wasting), 더 많은 에너지를 투자할 수 있었다.
det.analysis: waste(동사: 낭비하다) → wasting(동명사). 전치사 By 뒤에 동명사 필요.
det.tip: By + -ing = ~함으로써. 전치사 뒤에는 동명사. By wasting less = 덜 낭비함으로써

questions.passage: People say you shouldn't compare apples to oranges, and they're right. Maybe they had an advantage, or even a disadvantage, that you didn't. __________ Only you know where you started and how much effort you've put in.
questions.stem:
(정답은 **영어**로 작성) 다음 주어진 단어를 모두 사용하여 빈칸에 들어갈 문장을 완성하시오. (대소문자 구분 없음, 마침표 생략 가능)

[ the / only / fair / comparison / is / yesterday-you ]
questions.wa: the only fair comparison is yesterday-you
accept: the only fair comparison is yesterday-you
The only fair comparison is yesterday-you
the only fair comparison is yesterday-you.
The only fair comparison is yesterday-you.

det.korean: 유일하게 공정한 비교는 '어제의 나'이다.
det.analysis: the only fair comparison(S) + is(V) + yesterday-you(C): SVC 구조.
det.tip: the only fair comparison is 'yesterday-you' = 핵심 문장. 유일하게 공정한 비교 대상 = 과거의 나

questions.stem:
(정답은 **영어**로 작성) 다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 빈칸을 채우시오.

"나는 다른 사람들과만 비교했을 때 내 능력의 발전을 볼 수 없었다."

I couldn't see the __________ in my ability when I only compared myself to others.

det.korean: 내 능력의 발전(progress)을 볼 수 없었다.
det.analysis: 원문 'I couldn't see the progress in my ability'에서 progress를 찾아 쓰는 문제.
det.tip: progress = 발전, 진전. the progress in my ability = 내 능력의 발전

questions.stem:
(정답은 **영어**로 작성) 다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 빈칸을 채우시오.

"나는 더 이상 친구들이 어떻게 생각하는지 걱정하지 않고, 내 자신의 행동에 집중한다."

I no longer worry about what my friends think, and I __________ on my own actions.

det.korean: 나는 내 자신의 행동에 집중한다(focus).
det.analysis: 원문 'I focus on my own actions'에서 focus를 찾아 쓰는 문제.
det.tip: focus on = ~에 집중하다. focus on my own actions = 내 자신의 행동에 집중하다
